name: QCT / Quanta Cloud Technology GPGPU servers (ODM route)
region: QCT publishes a where-to-buy map with per-country partner counts: United States 9, Japan 6, Canada 4, Germany 3, Turkey 3, China 3, South Korea 3, Singapore 2, Switzerland 2, Brazil/Australia/India/Israel/Italy/Malaysia/Mexico/Netherlands/New Zealand/Philippines/Slovenia/Taiwan/Turkey 1 each; Denmark, Finland, France, Norway, Kazakhstan, Philippines, Poland, Portugal, Russia, Slovakia, Spain, Sweden, Ukraine and UAE show 0
notes:
QUOTE-ONLY. The distinctive and reusable finding here is that QCT, a hyperscale ODM, publishes an explicit reseller/SI channel map by COUNTRY, with partner counts per territory and partner types separated into 'Distributor', 'Distributor / Reseller / System Integrator', 'Reseller / System Integrator', and 'Reseller / System Integrator'. Named examples visible include Siselectron (Duluth GA) and Cambridge Computer (Waltham MA), both US resellers/SIs. Two things this is good for: (1) it is the clearest published evidence that the ODM accelerator route is reseller-mediated rather than direct, and (2) the zero-count countries are a hard constraint - an enterprise in, say, Spain, Spain-count 0, or the UAE, count 0, has no local QCT channel listed at all and must go through a US or EU partner, which changes lead time and support model. QCT's product taxonomy includes an explicit 'GPGPU' rackmount class. Accelerators arrive with the configured system, not as separable SKUs. Note the 'coming soon' tag appearing on some QCT listings: even at the ODM layer new accelerator generations are announced ahead of shippable product. EXPORT CONTROLLED (true). Regime: US BIS advanced-computing export controls (the Oct 2023 interim final rule, 88 FR 73458 - source sup-buy-bis-2023-advanced-computing-controls), which put datacenter accelerators under ECCN 3A090/4A090, added the advanced-computing Foreign Direct Product (FDP) rule, and extended Regional Stability (RS) controls to Country Groups D:1, D:4 and D:5. For items destined to Macau or Country Group D:5 the rule applies a PRESUMPTION OF DENIAL; other RS destinations get a presumption of approval. Practical effect: which accelerator you can legally be sold, and which SKU counts as compliant, is set by destination and end user - not by the channel.

 LEAD TIME: null and it is an EXPLICIT NEGATIVE, checked 2026-10-04. This is a quote-only channel - no price and no lead time is published on any page, and AGENTS.md forbids inventing an unsourced number, so the field stays null with the reason recorded. The negative is itself a procurement fact: a channel that will not state a lead time is a channel where the lead time is set by whatever allocation you happen to have, and it is exactly the kind of number to ask for in writing before signing. Probe log and per-vendor detail in source spl-negative-no-oem-publishes-lead-time; the one figure published anywhere in this chain is AWS's 8-week MAXIMUM Capacity Block booking horizon, which is a commitment ceiling rather than a delivery time.
